title: Transport essential-variable division to the full coefficient series
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $L$ a field in any universe, $m,n,s\in\mathbf N$, and $\alpha:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to\mathbf N^n$ an ordered vertex family for $D$ [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. Let $c_{i\gamma}\in A$, $e:A\to L$ a ring map, and $f_i\in L[[W_1,\ldots,W_m,Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]]$ such that $[W^0Z^\gamma]f_i=e(c_{i\gamma})$ for every $i,\gamma$. Use the restricted forms $h_{i,q}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-division-data]. Suppose $e_*(h_{i,q})$ have unique supported homogeneous division for every prefix $q$ and degree $t$. Then the degree-$|\alpha_i|$ homogeneous components of $\operatorname{truncTotal}(|\alpha_i|+1)(f_i)$ have unique supported homogeneous division in every degree and every prefix, in all $(W,Z)$ variables, with diagram and first-vertex supports determined by the full vertices $(0,\alpha_i)$. No lower order or first exponent of the $f_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: Enumerate the retained vertex subtype increasingly by a finite ordinal. Split the full variable set into the essential Z variables and their complement and enumerate both by finite ordinals. The resulting bijections transport exponent degree, coordinatewise divisibility, the first-dividing-vertex rule and finitely supported linear combinations.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. proof.text: Setting the complementary variables to zero in the degree-d_i form keeps exactly its essential-variable coefficients at W=0. The supplied coefficient identities identify this restriction with the mapped restrictedCoefficientForms. The degree-d_i homogeneous component of truncTotal(d_i+1) has exactly the degree-d_i coefficients of f_i.

proof.text: The ordered vertex hypothesis implies distinctness. Apply hasUniqueDivision_extraVariables_iff in the enumerated variables and transport the unique coefficients back. FullVertex preserves degree, so the full prefix and the retained original prefix identify. Empty index and variable sets use the same argument.
